overview: Black leaves e5 undefended and meets 3.Nxe5 with ...Nc6 (Chiodini Gambit) or the bishop sacrifice ...Bxf2+. White takes the pawn and then has to survive threats on f2 and the king; if White declines or trades cleanly, Black is simply a pawn down. Black plays for quick development and tricks on f2, with little sound compensation.

white_ideas.idea: Take e5 with the knight and then trade or kick the Nc6 to cash in the extra pawn
Meet ...Bxf2+ with Kxf2 and keep the king safe, returning material if needed
Develop quickly with d4 or Nxc6

black_ideas.idea: Use the f2 weakness and ...Nc6 for development in return for the e5 pawn
Piece sacrifice on f2 for an exposed king

typical_structures.structure: White a pawn up with Black pieces developed and no central pawn

character.notes: Black takes risks for development and tricks; one wrong White move gives Black attacking chances. Concrete tactics on f2 and the e-file.

gambit.notes: White can take e5 and keep it; Black must justify with development.

soundness.notes: Dubious; White can safely take the pawn.

approach.notes: Offbeat; strong players do not choose 2...Bc5 as Black.

level.notes: Easy to learn but dubious, so never beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: Chiodini Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Bc5 3. Nxe5 Nc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers the pawn and plays on development; if 4.Nxc6 dxc6 White is simply a pawn up.

character.reason: Gambit lines with tricks on f2 and the e-file.

gambit.reason: Black allows Nxe5 and plays for development.

soundness.reason: White can keep the pawn with little risk.

level.reason: Dubious gambit, not a beginner choice.

plans.reason: Black plays for development in return for a pawn.
